input_domain: Unmodified reference constructor and generic validator; bare direct owner constructor, not PBS input or a normal user name dialog.
Inputs are bounded ordinary integers or ordinary text; no custom equality/hash behavior.
No plugin wrappers or extra schema validation.
Other constructor fields are integers and dependencies for type validation are present.
premises_and_counterexample.ordinary_control: The formal failure clause says a constructor field type mismatch raises an error. Source groups type conditions by argument value; equal values keep the later condition. A numeric name equal to later integer gender/language therefore loses its text requirement and is stored as an integer. The individual name setter still rejects numeric input because its single check cannot be masked.

contrasts.result: ArgumentError; name0 does not merge with later integer fields

failure_cancel_partial_commit.cancel_exception_partial_commit: No interactive cancellation here. Rejected constructor input fails before all four field writes; accepted colliding input writes all four values unchanged. Individual name-setter rejection occurs before name mutation. No game/save execution or new transaction guarantee is asserted. Existing owner input in creature creation is accepted as the owner record; malformed internal name is not recursively rejected there.

premises_and_counterexample.impact: Incorrect static failure requirement and cross-field type invariant at the author-facing constructor boundary; a later clean-room validator that checks every field will behave differently on this reference counterexample. This does not require preserving malformed-name acceptance in the future product.
